barca.name: Barca
barca.blurb: A small, single-masted coaster with a square sail. Cheap to buy and run, but she keeps within sight of the coast: no Madeira, no open-sea passages. Corsairs seldom think her worth the trouble.

caravel.name: Caravel
caravel.blurb: Two lateen masts and a shallow draft. The best ship afloat for beating home against the trade winds.

barinel.name: Barinel
barinel.blurb: A broad oared sailing ship. Sweeps keep her moving at about 2 knots in a calm, as in the Gulf of Guinea.

largecaravel.name: Large caravel
largecaravel.blurb: A caravela latina grande: three lateen masts on a longer hull. More hold than a caravel and even closer to the wind.

redonda.name: Caravela redonda
redonda.blurb: A caravel with square sails on her fore and main masts and a lateen mizzen: fast with the wind behind her, a little slower into it.

nau.name: Nau
nau.blurb: A great carrack with high castles fore and aft. A huge hold and room for bombards; slow to windward. Galleys think twice before taking her on.

naudaindia.name: Nau da Índia
naudaindia.blurb: A great carrack built for the Carreira da Índia: four decks, a vast hold for pepper, and room for a hundred men. Clumsy to windward and too deep for most African ports, but nothing else carries so much round the Cape.

holk.name: Holk
holk.blurb: The big cargo ship of the Hanse and the North Sea: clinker-built, round and deep, with one great square sail. Roomy and cheap for her hold, slow and poor to windward. Built only in the northern yards.

carrack.name: Carrack
carrack.blurb: A great Genoese merchant ship, high-sided and hard to board, with a fighting top on her mainmast.

merchantman.name: Armed merchantman
merchantman.blurb: An English or Dutch trader with a row of guns: fast, and dangerous to hunt.

urca.name: Urca
urca.blurb: A Flemish hulk, broad and round, built to carry grain and salt cheaply. The most hold for the money, but slow, poor to windward, and a fat prize: corsairs like the look of her.

armedcaravel.name: Caravela de armada
armedcaravel.blurb: A four-masted caravel built for the crown's coast guard: a square sail on the foremast, three lateens, guns low in the hull. Little hold, but fast and dangerous: an escort, and a hunter of corsairs.

naovizcaina.name: Nao vizcaína
naovizcaina.blurb: A Basque cargo ship from the yards of Biscay, bought for the Andalusian trade: a deep round hull, a big square mainsail. Cheap for her hold, slow, and poor into the wind.

naocarrera.name: Nao de la Carrera
naocarrera.blurb: A nao built for the Indies run from Seville: a big hold for wine, oil and cloth out and sugar and hides home. Too deep for the river laden: she loads at Sanlúcar or Cádiz.

galeon.name: Galeón
galeon.blurb: The guard and treasure ship of the Indies fleets: long, low and gunned, and fast for her size.

galeao.name: Galleon
galeao.blurb: A long, low warship-merchantman with a beaked bow and four masts: faster and handier than a nau, with gun decks that make corsairs keep their distance.

choices.name: Coarse hemp
choices.note: Heavy and baggy.

choices.name: Breton canvas
choices.note: Good canvas from Olonne: the standard.

choices.name: Fine linen
choices.note: Light, close-woven sails that hold their shape.

choices.name: Topsails and topgallants
choices.note: Sails set above the main and fore courses, as the Flemings and English now rig them: more canvas aloft with the wind behind her.

choices.name: Bonnets laced on
choices.note: Extra strips of canvas laced to the foot of the sails in fair weather. More hands to work them.

choices.name: Spritsail and extra mizzen
choices.note: Small sails at bow and stern to balance her as she comes about.

choices.name: Careened and tallowed
choices.note: Hauled down, scraped of weed and coated with tallow and pitch. Lasts about six months.

choices.name: Extra stowage
choices.note: A new orlop deck and better racking below.

choices.name: Swivel guns (berços)
choices.note: Light breech-loaders on the rails.

choices.name: Falconets
choices.note: Small iron guns on carriages, firing a ball the size of a fist: a galley thinks twice before closing.

choices.name: Bombards
choices.note: Heavy guns on the main deck. Only a nau, a galleon or a nau da Índia can carry them.

choices.name: Bronze culverins
choices.note: Long bronze guns cast in the royal foundries, reaching twice as far as a bombard: she can hurt a galley before it closes. Only a nau, galleon or nau da Índia can carry them.

choices.name: Gunports and heavy guns
choices.note: Ports cut low in the hull, with lids, so heavy guns can ride below the deck without making her top-heavy. The new way of arming a ship.

choices.name: Crossbowmen
choices.note: A dozen crossbowmen, paid by the day, to sweep a galley's deck as she closes.

choices.name: Espingardeiros
choices.note: A dozen men with matchlock handguns (espingardas): slower to load than a crossbow, but they pierce mail.

choices.name: Men-at-arms
choices.note: Soldiers in mail with pikes and crossbows, enough to board a galley and take her.

choices.name: Boarding nets and pavises
choices.note: Nets rigged above the rails and wooden shields along them. Boarders struggle to get aboard, and to get off again with your goods.

choices.name: Better casks and dunnage
choices.note: Tight cooperage, and cargo kept off the wet bilge.

choices.name: A quadrant
choices.note: Her pilot takes the height of the Pole Star and knows how far south she is: she keeps a truer course and runs from bad weather sooner. Storms do her less harm.

choices.name: Astrolabe and the Regiment of the Sun
choices.note: A brass mariner's astrolabe and the king's tables of the sun's declination: latitude by day, south of the line where the Pole Star is gone.

choices.name: Zacuto's almanac
choices.note: Abraão Zacuto's tables, printed at Leiria, with a good astrolabe and a pilot trained to use them: the best a pilot can have.

choices.name: Lead sheathing
choices.note: Thin sheets of lead nailed over the hull below the waterline, against the shipworm of the tropics. She wears and ages more slowly in hot waters.

choices.name: Bigger pumps and a well
choices.note: Larger pumps and a proper pump well: a leaking hull spoils half as much cargo.

choices.name: Cross of the Order of Christ
Carved and gilded, with a name board
